name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: The dumbbell side bend trains lateral flexion of the spine against a unilateral resistance load, primarily targeting the obliques and quadratus lumborum on the working side while the contralateral side resists gravitational pull isometrically. The exercise is commonly performed with a single dumbbell in one hand, allowing a full lateral range of motion. It is important to perform the exercise bilaterally to avoid asymmetrical development.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in one hand at the side, feet shoulder-width apart, free hand placed lightly behind the head or on the hip.
execution.setup_instructions: Choose a moderate weight — excessive load encourages compensation through the hips rather than pure lateral spinal flexion.
steps: Step 1: Stand tall with the dumbbell at the side, spine neutral.
Step 2: Laterally flex the spine toward the dumbbell side, lowering the weight along the outer thigh.
Step 3: Return to upright by contracting the opposite-side obliques.
Step 4: Optionally continue past neutral to the opposite side for a full range of motion bend.
Step 5: Complete all reps then switch the dumbbell to the other hand.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale at neutral. Exhale as returning to upright.
common_mistakes: Bending forward or backward instead of purely laterally
Rotating the torso — the movement should be in the frontal plane only
safety_considerations: Use controlled movement — avoid lateral flexion under load with momentum
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full comfortable lateral flexion range on each side. Quality of movement over depth.
coaching_cues: Slide the dumbbell down the leg — no rotation
Think of your spine as a hinge opening sideways
